_note: Computer-state dialogue. system_watcher.py produces the tags (what app is in front, what the machine is doing, how long you have been at it); these files supply the lines. Editing this file changes what the pets say without touching Python.
_shape: states.<tag> is a list of general lines for that tag, or an object {event: [lines], '*': [lines]}. CAREFUL: a plain list answers EVERY event, not just idle chatter - while the tag is active a poke or a jump would use it too. To make these ordinary chatter, scope them: { "idle": [ ... ] }.
_events: 'state_enter' fires once when a tag starts being active (opening Genshin again), 'state_exit' once when it stops. Those two are the natural home for a tag's best lines; see _template.json.
_priority_order_note: Most important first. When several tags are active only the first one with a line pool is used, and the engine walks down this list until a pool has a line. Urgent machine problems sit at the top, specific apps beat general ones, and time of day is last because it is always on.
_priority_order_note_2: Anything not listed here is ranked BELOW everything listed, which is almost never what you want - system_watcher.py prints a startup note naming the tags it can emit that this list omits. Put a tag in this list when you add a pool for it.
_pools_note: The pools below are starters, in the default Sensei voice. They are scoped to "idle" (and "state_enter" / "state_exit") so a poke is still a poke - see _priority_order_note and data/README.md. Delete anything you do not want; a tag with no pool here falls through to the archetype and character files, then to the plain event lines.
